 Order

1. Vide this order, I shall adjudicate the Criminal Revision filed by revisionist namely Vimal Verma for seeking setting aside of impugned order dated 30.11.2024 passed by Ld. Trial Court in FIR No.
317/2023, PS- H.N. Din titled State Vs. Vimal Verma & Ors. by which Ld. Trial Court had dismissed the application moved on behalf of applicant/ accused Vimal Verma for seeking release of articles on superdari.

sentences.text: 2. Revisionist herein is the accused before Ld. Trial Court.
In my subsequent paragraphs, he will be referred with the same nomenclature with which he was referred before Ld. Trial Court, in order to avoid confusion.

3. The factual backdrop giving rise to the present revision petition is that accused/ revisionist had moved an application before Ld. Trial Court on 29.10.2024 for release of articles mentioned as below :-
1. One mobile phone (make Samsung), one Oppo Vivo, one Redmi.
2. Gold Chain.
3. Gold Ring.
4. Wrist Watch.
5. Purse Containing cash of Rs. 9600/-, PAN Card, Aadhar Card, Driving Licence, RC of vehicle No. DL3SVV 5674, ATM Card of Axis Bank, ATM Card of Indian Overseas Bank.
And also to allow the concerned authority to re-open the SIM Cards of aforesaid three mobile phones.

sentences.text: To the aforesaid application of superdari, reply was filed on behalf of IO wherein it has been stated that accused/ revisionist had been arrested on 29.10.2023.
One Samsung Galaxy S23 Cream Colour Mobile Phone, One Redmi Note 8 Blue Colour have IMEI No. 868269042816522
were seized during investigation and have been sent to FSL for opinion and the result of the same is awaited.
Further, no item was seized from the personal search of the accused/ revisionist.
Further, SIM Cards bearing nos. 9818681674, 9818969574, 9899772274, 9818407974 and 8368356625 were never recovered or seized during the investigation.

5. Upon the aforesaid application, Ld. Trial Court had passed impugned order dated 30.11.2024 by which it has been stated that the two mobile phones of make Samsung and Redmi have been sent to FSL and are required for investigation and trial.

Further, that mobile phone make Oppo was never seized and further that no SIM Cards were seized and therefore, cannot be released to the accused/
revisionist.

Further, it has been stated by Ld. Trial Court in the aforesaid impugned order that re-opening of the SIM Cards can also not be allowed as the same is beyond the scope of the application and hence the application of the accused/ revisionist, was dismissed.

6. It has been argued on behalf of accused/ revisionist that the aforesaid articles were seized by the IO on 29.10.2023 and out of the three mobile phones, only two mobile phones have been sent to FSL and the third mobile phone make Vivo has not been put on record by IO CR No. 786/2024 Vimal Vimal Verma vs State on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130119235/
2 Verma Vs. State Page No.3 of 6 anywhere in the charge-sheet.

It has further been argued that during the seizure memo of the mobile phones, even the SIM Cards were seized and the same are required by accused/ revisionist to carry on his business activities and the same is causing hardship to him.

It has also been argued that the present revision petition has been filed primarily for seeking permission for activation of the aforesaid SIM Cards for the accused/ revisionist to carry on his business.
7. Ld. Addl. PP for the State has argued that there is no infirmity in the impugned order of Ld. Trial Court and the present revision petition is liable to be dismissed.
8. I have heard Ld. Counsel for revisionist/ accused, Ld. Addl. PP for the State and have carefully perused the record.
9. On perusal of the record of Ld. Trial Court, it is seen that seizure memo dated 29.10.2023 shows that five passports were seized from the possession of accused/ revisionist.

Another seizure memo dated 29.10.2023 shows that only two mobile phones i.e. One Samsung Galaxy S23 Cream Colour having IMEI No. 3527725201143098 and 352814740143092 and another mobile phone make Redmi Note 8, blue colour having IMEI No. 868269042816522 and 868269042816530 were recovered from the possession of accused/ revisionist and apart from the aforesaid mobile phones,
no other articles were seized.

Further, the personal search memo of the accused/ revisionist dated 29.10.2023 also shows that no articles were recovered from the CR No. 786/2024 Vimal Verma Vs.
State Page No.4 of 6 personal search of the accused/ revisionist.

sentences.text:
Therefore, the aforesaid application moved on behalf of accused/ revisionist before Ld. Trial Court has been decided on the basis of seizure memos and the personal search memo and therefore, the application moved on behalf of accused/ revisionist for release of articles like one Oppo Vivo, Gold Chain, Gold Ring, Wrist Watch,
Purse Containing cash of Rs. 9600/-, PAN Card, Aadhar Card, Driving Licence, RC of vehicle No.
DL3S VB 5674, ATM Card of Axis Bank, ATM Card of Indian Overseas Bank,
is not maintainable and has been rightly dismissed by Ld. Trial Court.

Further, the mobile phone of make Samsung and Redmi are required for investigation and trial as the same have been sent to FSL and is the case property of the present matter and therefore, cannot be released to the accused/ revisionist.

10. Further, the contentions raised by accused/ revisionist for re- activation of SIM Cards has also been rightly dismissed by Ld. Trial Court as the same is not within the purview of the application moved on behalf of accused/ revisionist before Ld. Trial Court.
11. Keeping in view the aforesaid appreciation, I am of the considered view that Ld. Trial Court rightly passed the order dated 30.11.2024.

More so where, accused/ revisionist failed to give any cogent reason regarding any shortcoming in the application of mind by Ld. Magistrate while passing impugned order, I find that present revision petition is meritless.

Impugned order has reasons,
which are not repeated here for the sake of brevity.
Those reasons were outcome CR No. 786/2024 Vimal Verma Vs. State Page No.5 of 6 of proper exercise of judicial discretion and is not an arbitrary order and not passed in a mechanical manner.

Accordingly, present revision petition, stands dismissed.
